grammar: n. 西瓜。可数名词；切开后可说 a slice/piece of watermelon。
collocations: a slice of watermelon; watermelon juice; a ripe watermelon
commonMistake: watermelon 可指一个完整的西瓜，也可指西瓜果肉；说一片时常用 a slice of watermelon。

example.english: We shared a slice of watermelon after the game.
example.chinese: 比赛后我们分吃了一片西瓜。

application.prompt: This large green fruit has red flesh and black seeds. It is a ___. (watermelon / cabbage)

grammar: n. 卷心菜。可数名词，复数 cabbages；做菜时也常说 some cabbage。
collocations: a head of cabbage; cabbage soup; chopped cabbage
commonMistake: cabbage 是可数名词，完整的一棵可说 a cabbage；一颗完整卷心菜也常说 a head of cabbage。

example.english: We add some cabbage to the soup.
example.chinese: 我们往汤里加一些卷心菜。

application.prompt: This leafy vegetable is often used in coleslaw. It is a ___. (cabbage / mutton)

grammar: n. 羊肉。通常作不可数名词；表示一份可说 a piece of mutton。
collocations: mutton soup; a piece of mutton; cook mutton slowly
commonMistake: mutton 指羊肉时通常不可数，不说 a mutton 或 muttons；表示一只羊常用 sheep。

example.english: The restaurant serves mutton soup on cold days.
example.chinese: 这家餐馆在寒冷的日子里供应羊肉汤。

application.prompt: The soup is made with meat from a sheep: ___. (mutton / strawberry)

grammar: n. 曲奇饼。可数名词，复数 cookies；在美式英语中常用 cookie，英式英语中 biscuit 也很常见。
collocations: a chocolate-chip cookie; a cookie jar; bake cookies
commonMistake: cookie 是可数名词，单数前通常要有 a/an/the；多个要用 cookies。

example.english: I packed two cookies for the school trip.
example.chinese: 我为学校旅行装了两块曲奇饼。

application.prompt: A small sweet biscuit with chocolate chips is a ___. (cookie / onion)

grammar: n. 洋葱；葱头。可数名词，复数 onions；切片可说 slices of onion。
collocations: a red onion; chop an onion; onion soup
commonMistake: onion 是可数名词；单数前用 a，因为 onion 以元音音素开头。

example.english: Please chop an onion for the salad.
example.chinese: 请切一个洋葱做沙拉。

application.prompt: This vegetable has layers and can make your eyes water when cut: an ___. (onion / porridge)

grammar: n. 饺子。可数名词，复数 dumplings；可指煮、蒸或煎的带馅面食。
collocations: make dumplings; boil dumplings; a plate of dumplings
commonMistake: dumpling 是可数名词；表示一盘时说 a plate of dumplings。

example.english: My family makes dumplings together on Sunday.
example.chinese: 星期天我们一家人一起包饺子。

application.prompt: A boiled or steamed parcel of dough with a filling is a ___. (dumpling / pear)

grammar: n. 咖啡。通常作不可数名词；a coffee 可表示一杯咖啡，a cup of coffee 也很常见。
collocations: a cup of coffee; black coffee; drink coffee
commonMistake: 泛指咖啡饮料时通常不加 a；点一杯时可说 a coffee 或 a cup of coffee。

example.english: My father drinks a cup of coffee after breakfast.
example.chinese: 我爸爸早餐后喝一杯咖啡。

application.prompt: I drink a cup of ___ to wake up in the morning. (coffee / bean)

grammar: n. 豆。可数名词，复数 beans；常指一粒豆，也可用于 green beans 等食物名称。
collocations: green beans; coffee beans; a can of beans
commonMistake: bean 是可数名词，一粒豆说 a bean，多粒说 beans；泛指一份豆子也可说 some beans。

example.english: We put green beans in the vegetable salad.
example.chinese: 我们把青豆放进蔬菜沙拉里。

application.prompt: A coffee ___ is a seed used to make coffee. (bean / cookie)

grammar: n. 炸薯条。英式英语中 chips 常指较粗的炸土豆条；美式英语中的 chip 常指薄脆薯片。
collocations: fish and chips; a portion of chips; hot chips
commonMistake: 按本课英式用法，chips 指炸薯条；美式英语常把薄脆薯片叫 chips。

example.english: We ordered hot chips with our fish.
example.chinese: 我们点的鱼配了热薯条。

application.prompt: On a British menu, fish is often served with fried potato pieces called ___. (chips / cookies)

grammar: 短语名词，炸鱼薯条；通常作不可数的菜名，fish 指炸鱼，chips 指炸薯条。
collocations: order fish and chips; a portion of fish and chips; fish-and-chips shop
commonMistake: fish and chips 是固定菜名；泛指这道菜通常不把 fish 改成 fishes。

example.english: We had fish and chips for lunch by the sea.
example.chinese: 我们在海边吃了炸鱼薯条作午餐。

application.prompt: A meal of battered fried fish with fried potato strips is called ___. (fish and chips / salad)

grammar: n. 沙拉；色拉。可指一份沙拉，也可泛指沙拉食材；可数用法复数 salads。
collocations: a fruit salad; a green salad; make a salad
commonMistake: salad 可数时单数前要有冠词，如 a salad；泛指沙拉食材时也可说 some salad。

example.english: I made a fruit salad with apples and strawberries.
example.chinese: 我用苹果和草莓做了一份水果沙拉。

application.prompt: A cold dish made with mixed vegetables or fruit is a ___. (salad / mutton)

grammar: n. 粥；麦片粥。通常作不可数名词；表示一碗可说 a bowl of porridge。
collocations: a bowl of porridge; eat porridge for breakfast; cook porridge
commonMistake: porridge 通常不可数，不说 a porridge；要数一碗时说 a bowl of porridge。

example.english: We eat porridge for breakfast on cold mornings.
example.chinese: 寒冷的早晨我们早餐吃粥。

application.prompt: A warm breakfast made by cooking oats in water or milk is ___. (porridge / chips)

grammar: n. （男）服务员。可数名词，复数 waiters；server 是不强调性别的常见说法。
collocations: ask the waiter; a restaurant waiter; waiter service
commonMistake: waiter 按本词表指男服务员；waitress 指女服务员，server 可作不强调性别的称呼。

example.english: The waiter brought us the menu.
example.chinese: 服务员把菜单拿给了我们。

application.prompt: The male restaurant worker who takes your order is a ___. (waiter / customer)

grammar: 短语，用于征求意见或提出建议；后接名词，也可接动词-ing，如 What about ordering soup?。
collocations: What about some tea?; What about a salad?; What about trying the soup?
commonMistake: What about 后接名词或动词-ing，不接 to do；提出建议时也可用 How about。

example.english: “What about some soup?” “That sounds good.”
example.chinese: “来点汤怎么样？”“听起来不错。”

application.prompt: Suggest ordering a salad: “___ ordering a salad?” (What about / What to)

sources.label: Cambridge Grammar: suggestions with what about

grammar: v. 有……味道；尝；n. 味道。作系动词时后接形容词，如 taste sweet；作名词时可用 a taste of。
collocations: taste sweet; taste the soup; a salty taste
commonMistake: taste 作系动词描述味道时用形容词，如 taste salty；味道是 salty，不说 taste salt。

example.english: The soup tastes salty, so I add some water.
example.chinese: 汤尝起来很咸，所以我加了些水。

application.prompt: The soup has a salty ___. (taste / menu)

grammar: pron. 某事物；任何事物。常用于疑问句和否定句；肯定句中可表示“任何东西”。
collocations: anything else; don’t eat anything; anything you like
commonMistake: anything 作代词，后面通常不再接 thing；形容词放在 anything 后，如 anything else。

example.english: Would you like anything else from the menu?
example.chinese: 菜单上你还想要别的什么吗？

application.prompt: We have no dessert left, so we don’t have ___ else to serve. (anything / something)

grammar: n. 一道菜；盘子。可数名词，复数 dishes；具体含义由点餐或餐具语境判断。
collocations: a chicken dish; wash the dishes; a dish of noodles
commonMistake: dish 可指一道菜，也可指盛食物的盘子；复数 dishes 的结尾加 -es。

example.english: This restaurant is famous for a spicy chicken dish.
example.chinese: 这家餐馆以一道辣鸡肉菜闻名。

application.prompt: A prepared item of food on a menu, rather than the plate it is served on, is a ___. (dish / menu)

grammar: n. 选择；可数名词，复数 choices。常用 make a choice、a choice between A and B、a choice of。
collocations: make a choice; a healthy choice; a choice between tea and coffee
commonMistake: choice 是名词，动词是 choose；选择某物说 choose sth，作名词说 make a choice。

example.english: Fruit is a good choice for an afternoon snack.
example.chinese: 水果是不错的下午点心选择。

application.prompt: You can have tea or coffee; you have a ___ to make. (choice / meal)

grammar: n. 一餐所吃的食物；一餐。可数名词，常指早餐、午餐、晚餐或某次用餐。
collocations: have a meal; a healthy meal; breakfast is a meal
commonMistake: meal 指一餐或这一餐的食物；dish 指一道菜，二者不完全相同。

example.english: Breakfast is an important meal for many families.
example.chinese: 对许多家庭来说，早餐是一顿重要的餐食。

application.prompt: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are each a ___. (meal / dish)

grammar: n. 猪肉。通常作不可数名词；可说 a piece of pork 或 some pork。
collocations: pork soup; a piece of pork; cook pork thoroughly
commonMistake: pork 指猪肉时通常不可数，不说 a pork 或 porks；数份量时用 piece/pieces。

example.english: The menu has pork with rice and vegetables.
example.chinese: 菜单上有猪肉配米饭和蔬菜。

application.prompt: This soup contains meat from a pig: ___. (pork / mutton)

grammar: n. 草莓。可数名词，复数 strawberries；辅音字母 + y 结尾变复数时 y 改为 ies。
collocations: a strawberry; fresh strawberries; strawberry jam
commonMistake: strawberry 的复数是 strawberries，不是 strawberrys；一个草莓说 a strawberry。

example.english: She put three strawberries on the cake.
example.chinese: 她在蛋糕上放了三颗草莓。

application.prompt: One berry is a strawberry; two are two ___. (strawberries / strawberrys)

grammar: n. 菜单。可数名词，复数 menus；餐馆菜单列出可点的食物和饮料。
collocations: read the menu; a lunch menu; on the menu
commonMistake: menu 是可数名词，通常说 a menu 或 the menu；复数是 menus。

example.english: The soup of the day is on the menu.
example.chinese: 今日例汤在菜单上。

application.prompt: A list of food and drinks you can order at a restaurant is a ___. (menu / customer)

grammar: n. 顾客。可数名词，复数 customers；指购买商品或服务的人。
collocations: a regular customer; customer service; help a customer
commonMistake: customer 是购买商品或服务的人；custom 是“习俗”或“定制”，词义和词性不同。

example.english: The customer asked the waiter for a glass of water.
example.chinese: 顾客向服务员要了一杯水。

application.prompt: The person who buys a meal at a restaurant is a ___. (customer / waiter)

grammar: v. 提供；服务。serve—served—served；可用 serve sb sth 或 serve sth to sb。
collocations: serve lunch; serve food to customers; serve a meal
commonMistake: serve 可直接接人和食物：serve customers lunch；也可说 serve lunch to customers。

example.english: The café serves breakfast until ten o’clock.
example.chinese: 这家咖啡馆供应早餐到十点。

application.prompt: This restaurant ___ hot meals from noon to two. (serves / serve)

grammar: n. 女服务员。可数名词，复数 waitresses；不强调性别时可用 server。
collocations: ask the waitress; a restaurant waitress; waitress service
commonMistake: waitress 指女服务员；复数是 waitresses。waiter 是男服务员，server 可不强调性别。

example.english: The waitress brought our drinks to the table.
example.chinese: 女服务员把饮料端到了桌边。

application.prompt: The female restaurant worker who brings your food is a ___. (waitress / customer)

grammar: n. 先生；礼貌称呼男性顾客或陌生男子。直接称呼时常用在句末或句首。
collocations: Yes, sir.; excuse me, sir; thank you, sir
commonMistake: sir 作礼貌称呼时通常小写，如 Yes, sir；句首才首字母大写。

example.english: “Here is your menu, sir,” the waiter said.
example.chinese: “先生，这是您的菜单。”服务员说道。

application.prompt: A waiter politely addresses a male customer: “Would you like some water, ___?” (sir / madam)

grammar: 短语动词，搭配；相配。主语为第三人称单数时用 goes with；可表示食物或颜色相配。
collocations: go with soup; go well with rice; a dish that goes with salad
commonMistake: go with 表示两样东西相配；主语是单数时用 goes with，如 This dish goes with rice。

example.english: This salad goes well with the soup.
example.chinese: 这份沙拉和汤很相配。

application.prompt: Soup often goes ___ bread. (with / from)

grammar: adv. 反而；代替。可单独使用，常放在句末或句首；instead of 后接名词或动词-ing。
collocations: use this instead; instead of sugar; stay home instead
commonMistake: instead 单独使用；instead of 后接名词或动词-ing，不接动词原形直接构成不定式。

example.english: There was no pear pie, so we ordered apple pie instead.
example.chinese: 没有梨派，所以我们改点了苹果派。

application.prompt: The café has no soup today. ___, we can order a salad. (Instead / Among)

grammar: n. 梨。可数名词，复数 pears；常用于水果、果汁或甜点语境。
collocations: a ripe pear; pear juice; a pear pie
commonMistake: pear 是可数名词，单数前用 a；不要与同音词 pair（一双）混淆。

example.english: I packed a pear for my afternoon snack.
example.chinese: 我带了一个梨当下午点心。

application.prompt: A green or yellow fruit with a rounded bottom is a ___. (pear / bean)

grammar: 短语，太多；可修饰不可数名词，也可在动词后作数量代词。too much + 不可数名词；可数名词复数用 too many。
collocations: too much sugar; eat too much; too much salt in soup
commonMistake: too much 修饰不可数名词，如 too much salt；too many 修饰可数名词复数，如 too many cookies。

example.english: There is too much sugar in this drink.
example.chinese: 这杯饮料里的糖太多了。

application.prompt: There is ___ salt in this soup. (too much / too many)

sources.label: Cambridge Grammar: too and too much

grammar: n. 糖。通常作不可数名词；可说 a spoonful/cube of sugar。
collocations: add sugar; a spoonful of sugar; sugar in tea
commonMistake: 泛指糖时 sugar 不可数，不说 sugars；表示具体种类时才可能用复数。

example.english: Would you like a little sugar in your tea?
example.chinese: 你的茶里要加一点糖吗？

application.prompt: Please add one spoonful of ___, not salt. (sugar / sugars)

grammar: v. 改进；改善。可作及物或不及物动词；规则变化 improve—improved—improved。
collocations: improve a habit; improve your health; improve over time
commonMistake: improve 作动词，直接接被改进的事物；不说 improve about sth。

example.english: Small changes can improve our lunch choices.
example.chinese: 小小的改变可以改善我们的午餐选择。

application.prompt: We want to ___ our lunch choices by adding fruit. (improve / improving)

grammar: n. 习惯。可数名词，复数 habits；常用 have/develop a habit of doing sth。
collocations: a healthy habit; eating habits; break a habit
commonMistake: habit 是可数名词，单数前通常要有 a/the；说“做某事的习惯”常用 a habit of doing。

example.english: Eating breakfast before school is a good habit.
example.chinese: 上学前吃早餐是个好习惯。

application.prompt: Brushing your teeth after meals is a healthy ___. (habit / weight)

grammar: 短语名词，快餐。通常作不可数名词；fast-food 作复合形容词时可修饰 restaurant。
collocations: eat fast food; a fast-food restaurant; fast-food meal
commonMistake: 泛指快餐时通常不说 a fast food；修饰名词时可写 fast-food restaurant。

example.english: We do not eat fast food every day.
example.chinese: 我们不是每天都吃快餐。

application.prompt: Burgers and fries sold ready to eat are often called ___. (fast food / soft drink)

grammar: n. 盐。通常作不可数名词；可用 a pinch/spoonful of salt 表示少量。
collocations: a pinch of salt; add salt to soup; salt and pepper
commonMistake: salt 泛指盐时不可数，不说 a salt；需要表示具体量时用 a pinch of salt。

example.english: Add a pinch of salt to the soup.
example.chinese: 往汤里加一小撮盐。

application.prompt: The cook adds a pinch of ___ to the soup. (salt / cookie)

grammar: n. 脂肪；adj. 肥胖的。作名词可指食物中的脂肪，通常不可数；形容人时 fat 可能显得冒犯，使用时注意语境。
collocations: fat in food; low-fat milk; body fat
commonMistake: fat 作名词表示脂肪，作形容词表示肥胖的；描述食物营养时常说 the fat in food，避免用它随意评价他人外形。

example.english: The label shows how much fat is in the food.
example.chinese: 标签上标明了食物含有多少脂肪。

application.prompt: A nutrition label can show how much ___ is in a food. (fat / thirsty)

grammar: 短语动词，增加（体重）；穿上。put—put—put；表示穿衣时可分开，代词宾语放中间，如 put it on；put on weight 表示体重增加。
collocations: put on weight; put on a jacket; put your coat on
commonMistake: 表示“穿上”时可说 put on a coat 或 put it on；不能说 put on it。put on weight 不加冠词。

example.english: I put on my jacket before going outside.
example.chinese: 我出门前穿上了夹克。

application.prompt: If someone gains weight, we can say they ___ weight. (put on / go with)

grammar: n. 体重；重量。通常不可数；常用 the weight of sth、gain/lose weight。
collocations: body weight; the weight of a bag; gain weight
commonMistake: weight 是名词，weigh 是动词；说“体重增加”用 put on/gain weight。

example.english: The recipe lists the weight of each ingredient in grams.
example.chinese: 食谱用克标出了每种食材的重量。

application.prompt: The recipe lists the ___ of each ingredient in grams. (weight / weigh)

grammar: n. 汉堡包。可数名词，复数 hamburgers；常见缩写 burger。
collocations: a hamburger; a hamburger bun; order hamburgers
commonMistake: hamburger 是可数名词，单数前通常用 a；hamburger 也可指汉堡肉饼，但点餐时常指整个汉堡。

example.english: He ordered a hamburger and a glass of water.
example.chinese: 他点了一个汉堡包和一杯水。

application.prompt: A cooked patty served inside a bun is a ___. (hamburger / salad)

grammar: v. 造成；导致。cause—caused—caused；常用 cause sth 或 cause sb/sth to do sth。
collocations: cause a problem; cause a delay; cause sth to happen
commonMistake: cause 后可接名词或宾语 + to do：cause a delay、cause the bus to be late；不要与 because 混淆。

example.english: The broken fridge caused the ice cream to melt.
example.chinese: 冰箱坏了，导致冰淇淋融化。

application.prompt: Heavy rain may ___ the outdoor meal to start late. (cause / result)

grammar: n. 心脏；中心。可数名词，复数 hearts；heart 也可指某事物的中心或核心。
collocations: a healthy heart; the heart of the city; from the heart
commonMistake: heart 可指身体器官，也可比喻“中心”；不要与发音相近的 hear（听见）混淆。

example.english: The heart pumps blood around the body.
example.chinese: 心脏把血液泵送到全身。

application.prompt: The organ that pumps blood around the body is the ___. (heart / menu)

grammar: adj. 均衡的；平衡的。由 balance + -ed 构成；常修饰 diet、meal 或 lifestyle。
collocations: a balanced diet; a balanced meal; keep a balanced routine
commonMistake: balanced 是形容词；说“均衡饮食”用 a balanced diet。饮食平衡可看一天或一周，不必每餐都完全相同。

example.english: We planned a balanced lunch with rice, vegetables, and beans.
example.chinese: 我们安排了一顿有米饭、蔬菜和豆类的均衡午餐。

application.prompt: A meal with a suitable mix of different foods is a ___ meal. (balanced / sleepy)

grammar: 短语结构，太……以至于不能……：too + 形容词/副词 + to + 动词原形。
collocations: too hot to eat; too full to move; too tired to cook
commonMistake: too ... to 中两个部分都要有：too + adj. + to do；不要在 to 后用动词-ing。

example.english: The soup is too hot to eat now.
example.chinese: 这汤现在太烫了，不能吃。

application.prompt: The drink is ___ cold ___ drink quickly. Complete the “太……以至于不能……” pattern.

sources.label: Cambridge Grammar: too and too much

grammar: adj. 困倦的；想睡的。常用 feel/look sleepy；名词 sleep 表示睡眠。
collocations: feel sleepy; look sleepy; a sleepy child
commonMistake: sleepy 表示困倦，asleep 表示已经睡着；说 feel sleepy，不说 feel asleep。

example.english: I feel sleepy after staying up late.
example.chinese: 熬夜后我觉得困倦。

application.prompt: After a late night, I feel ___ during class. (sleepy / thirsty)

grammar: 短语，毕竟；终归。常用来补充一个重要事实或解释前面的判断。
collocations: after all, ...; it is not surprising after all; remember that, after all
commonMistake: after all 在这里表示“毕竟”，不是“在所有事情之后”；常用来补充理由或提醒事实。

example.english: Let’s share the fruit salad; after all, there is enough for everyone.
example.chinese: 我们一起分水果沙拉吧，毕竟足够每个人吃。

application.prompt: We can share the fruit salad; ___, there is enough for everyone. (After all / Instead)

grammar: adv. 离开；在别处；相隔。常见 go away、put sth away、a short distance away。
collocations: go away; two blocks away; put food away
commonMistake: away 可表示不在此处或相隔一段距离；说明距离时常放在距离词后，如 two miles away。

example.english: The café is only two blocks away from the school.
example.chinese: 咖啡馆离学校只有两个街区。

application.prompt: The café is two blocks ___ from the school. (away / instead)

grammar: adj. 不好的；贫穷的；可怜的。含义看语境；描述质量时可说 poor service/quality。
collocations: poor quality; poor service; a poor family
commonMistake: poor 可表示质量差或贫穷；描述服务或质量时可用 poor，但谈论人的经济状况时注意尊重。

example.english: The restaurant received poor reviews because its food was cold.
example.chinese: 这家餐馆因食物冷而收到差评。

application.prompt: The food was badly prepared; it was of ___ quality. (poor / balanced)

grammar: n. 后果；结果。可数名词，复数 results；常用 the result of sth、as a result。
collocations: the result of a test; as a result; get a good result
commonMistake: result 是名词；“导致”常用 result in，后接结果；“……的结果”用 the result of。

example.english: The result of the taste test was a tie.
example.chinese: 味觉测试的结果是平局。

application.prompt: The ___ of the taste test was a tie. (result / menu)

grammar: n. 文章；冠词。可数名词，复数 articles；语境可判断是报刊文章还是语法中的 a/an/the。
collocations: a newspaper article; read an article; an article in English grammar
commonMistake: article 可指文章，也可指冠词；a、an、the 是英语中的 articles。

example.english: I read an article about healthy school lunches.
example.chinese: 我读了一篇关于健康学校午餐的文章。

application.prompt: In “a pear,” the word “a” is an ___. (article / menu)

grammar: adj. 共同的；普遍的。可表示许多人或事物共有，也可表示经常发生、不稀奇。
collocations: a common mistake; a common problem; common interests
commonMistake: common 表示常见或共同，不等于“普通质量差”；名词形式 commonness 较少用，常用名词是 community（共同体/社区）。

example.english: A common lunch choice at our school is rice with vegetables.
example.chinese: 我们学校常见的午餐选择是米饭配蔬菜。

application.prompt: A mistake made by many learners is a ___ mistake. (common / balanced)

grammar: prep. 在……中；……之一。常用于三者或更多的人、事物组成的群体中。
collocations: among friends; among the choices; one among many
commonMistake: among 后接一个群体；between 常用于两个对象之间的关系，但也可用于多个明确区分的对象。

example.english: Among the dishes, the salad is my favourite.
example.chinese: 这些菜中，沙拉是我最喜欢的。

application.prompt: ___ all the dishes, the salad is my favourite. (Among / Before)

grammar: adj. 柔和的；柔软的。可描述触感、声音或食物质地；比较级 softer。
collocations: soft bread; a soft voice; soft cheese
commonMistake: soft 描述柔软或柔和；作副词通常用 softly，如 speak softly。

example.english: The bread is soft and easy to eat.
example.chinese: 面包很松软，容易吃。

application.prompt: A pillow that is not hard is ___. (soft / thirsty)

grammar: 短语名词，软饮料（不含酒精）。可数名词，复数 soft drinks。
collocations: a soft drink; cold soft drinks; order a soft drink
commonMistake: soft drink 指不含酒精的饮料，不表示“口感柔软的饮料”；单数前要有 a/the。

example.english: Would you like a soft drink with your meal?
example.chinese: 你用餐时想要一杯软饮料吗？

application.prompt: Cola is a cold, non-alcoholic ___. (soft drink / mutton)

grammar: adj. 足够的；adv. 足够地、充分地；pron. 足够。enough + 名词；形容词/副词 + enough；也可单独作代词。
collocations: enough food; warm enough; have had enough
commonMistake: enough 放名词前，如 enough water；放形容词后，如 warm enough；不说 enough warm。

example.english: We have enough fruit for everyone.
example.chinese: 我们的水果够每个人吃。

application.prompt: The soup is cool ___ for a child to eat. (enough / too)

grammar: adj. 渴的。常用 feel/be thirsty；thirsty for sth 也可表示“渴望得到某物”。
collocations: feel thirsty; get thirsty; thirsty for knowledge
commonMistake: thirsty 是形容词，常接 be/feel；名词是 thirst。

example.english: After PE, I felt thirsty and drank some water.
example.chinese: 体育课后我觉得口渴，喝了些水。

application.prompt: After running, I feel ___ and want a glass of water. (thirsty / sleepy)

grammar: 专有名词，宫保鸡丁；菜名中两个词首字母大写。也常见 Kung Pao chicken 的拼写。
collocations: order Gongbao chicken; a plate of Gongbao chicken; Gongbao chicken with rice
commonMistake: 菜名按本词表写作 Gongbao chicken，Gongbao 首字母大写；也可见 Kung Pao chicken 这一拼法。

example.english: Gongbao chicken is on the menu today.
example.chinese: 今天的菜单上有宫保鸡丁。

application.prompt: Choose the correctly capitalized dish name: (Gongbao chicken / gongbao Chicken)

sources.label: China Culture: Kung Pao chicken (Gong Bao chicken)

grammar: 专有名词，美国；美洲。首字母大写；语境通常可判断是美国还是美洲。
collocations: in America; travel to America; North America
commonMistake: America 是专有名词，首字母必须大写；在日常英语中常指美国，the Americas 指美洲。

example.english: My aunt lives in America and often visits us in summer.
example.chinese: 我姑妈住在美国，夏天常来看我们。

application.prompt: My aunt moved from China to the United States. She moved to ___. (America / Canada)

grammar: 专有名词，东坡肉；杭州传统菜名，Dongpo 首字母大写，pork 小写。
collocations: order Dongpo pork; a Hangzhou dish; Dongpo pork with rice
commonMistake: 按本词表写作 Dongpo pork，专有名称 Dongpo 大写，普通名词 pork 小写。

example.english: Dongpo pork is a well-known Hangzhou dish.
example.chinese: 东坡肉是杭州的知名菜肴。

application.prompt: Complete the name of this Hangzhou dish: Dongpo ___. (pork / chicken)
